html:
The Songhai Empire was the largest of the West African Sahel empires, ruled from Gao on the bend of the Niger from 1464 to 1591. A Songhai state had existed around Gao since the 1000s and was for a time subject to the Mali Empire.

  • Sonni Ali (ruled 1464 to 1492) built the empire by constant war, taking Timbuktu in 1468 and Djenné around 1475.
  • Askia Muhammad I (ruled 1493 to 1528) seized power and founded the Askia dynasty. He made the pilgrimage to Mecca, backed Muslim scholars, divided the empire into provinces and kept a standing army.
  • Later askias fought each other over the succession, which weakened the state.

Songhai grew rich on the trans-Saharan trade in gold, salt and slaves. Timbuktu and Djenné were its centres of trade and learning.

Its end came from the north. Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur of Morocco, of the Saadi dynasty, wanted control of the salt and gold trade. He sent an army of musketeers across the Sahara, and in 1591 it beat the much larger Songhai army at the Battle of Tondibi, guns against spears and cavalry. Morocco could not rule the region for long. It broke into small states, and the desert trade faded as Europeans bought gold on the Atlantic coast instead.
